title: Flo Master’s Top 5 Tips To Get Healthy In 2022
summary: Any day is a chance to make a change and get healthy! FightCamp Trainer Flo Master shares his top 5 tips for starting your 2022 right.
body_text: As a boxing coach and fitness professional, this is the time of year when I get a lot of questions about how to “get healthy” in the new year. People assume that I will hand them a detailed fitness and nutrition program, but proper health is more than just skin deep. The New Year is not the only opportunity to “get healthy.” You can start any time of the year! Flo Master’s Top 5 Tips To Get Healthy Here are my top five (5) tips for getting healthy in 2022 or any time of the year: 1. Keep It Simple Too often, people trying to make changes bite off more than they can chew. They change their diet, quit drinking alcohol, and start a new fitness routine , all in one swoop. Too many changes are hard to maintain, especially all at once. Frustration sets in and all new habits get thrown out the window. Lasting change happens slowly. Focus on making one change at a time. Then, once you feel comfortable with it, layer on the next. 2. Make Sleep a Priority Fighters take sleep and recovery very seriously. Lack of sleep leads to a foggy mind, bad choices, and a lack of energy. You can’t run a 5K if you are too tired to wake up and train. SLEEP! 3. Drink Water Like sleep, fighters and other athletes prioritize hydration. A hydrated body sleeps better, trains harder, and thinks faster. Taking in water also helps the body recover more efficiently by flushing out toxins. And, yes, drinking more water can help you shed weight. 4. Surround Yourself With the Right People Being around negative people can drain your energy and motivation. Spend your time with people who support your growth mindset , desire to be better, and celebrate your successes. 5. Determine Your “Why” It’s not enough to decide that you want to be healthier in 2022. There’s no motivation there. However, if you can tie a “why” to your goal , you have greater odds of achieving it. Some great reasons people want to get healthy are living pain-free, playing sports with their kids, climbing a mountain in Europe, or living to be 101. If you can come up with a clear reason why you want to get healthy this year and remind yourself of it daily, I promise that you’ll have tremendous success. Take Action How about you? Are you surprised that I don’t recommend doing 150 sit-ups every day? Getting healthy is not only what you see on the outside, but how you feel on the inside. Take some time to think about my five tips, write down a plan that works for you, and take action. I forgot the most important tip! You don’t have to worry if January 1st has already passed. You can start getting healthy any day of the year. I want to know if you take action on any or all of these tips. Join the conversation on FightCamp’s Facebook Community and let me know. Check out the FightCamp app and blog to help you start your fitness journey with workouts, step-by-step guides, and tips for nutrition and wellness.

FightCamp Releases 4 New Workout Collections
summary: FightCamp launches 4 NEW workout collections: Strength, Conditioning, Recovery & Stretch. More content to get you (and keep you) in fighting shape!
body_text: Just in time for the New Year, FightCamp has launched four (4) new workout collections on the App . These workouts focus on Strength, Conditioning, Recovery & Post-Workout Stretching. 4 Workout Collections Note : All four of these workout types are OPEN level, meaning that you do not need Punch Trackers. Strength Description : Bodyweight strength workouts to build muscle and power. Benefits : Strength training workouts not only are important for building muscle and tone, but also increase the range of motion and mobility of your joints. An added benefit of strength training is that it also helps protect you from injury. Conditioning Description : Cardio-based workouts to build speed, endurance, and stamina. Benefits : Conditioning workouts help with endurance, flexibility, and overall athletic performance. They help with developing more speed, balance, and coordination in addition to enhancing your overall training. Recovery Description : Dedicated sessions for your off days to help your body recover to perform at its peak. Benefits : Recovery workouts are essential for any athlete's training. They allow your muscles and body time to rest and rebuild so you can return to your training stronger. Post-Workout Stretch Description : Stretching sessions to increase flexibility. Benefits : Pre- and especially post-workout stretching is great for mobility and flexibility performance. Following your workout, focus on stretching the muscles you just trained to keep the range of motion in your joints and prevent them from becoming tight. Start Training! At FightCamp , we are always looking to take your at-home workouts to the next level. We are committed to helping you get (and stay) in shape through our on-demand boxing and kickboxing training. Now, we have added even more great content to our App and are delivering you with new (and fun) opportunities to work your muscles and enhance your routines. If you're looking for ways to amp up your workouts, try these new collections and let us know what you think in our Facebook Community . It's never too late to try something new--get started on your at-home fitness journey with FightCamp today!

title: Statement on COVID-19 Vaccine Clinical Studies in Children & Adolescents
summary: Deliver the greatest possible impact to people through mRNA medicines.
body_text: The U.S. FDA requested additional participants at a given dose level in pediatric cohorts after the VRBPAC review of requirements for pediatric EUA on June 10, 2021, and Moderna complied at that time. Outside the United States, Moderna has received regulatory authorizations in Europe, UK, Australia, and Canada for adolescents 12-17 years of age, and has submitted applications for 6-11 years of age. ﻿ In early December, Moderna also decided to evaluate the potential of lower doses to meet regulatory guidance for immunogenicity in children 6-11 years of age and in adolescents 12-17 years of age in our ongoing clinical trials. The Company is also evaluating a booster dose in adolescents 12-17 years of age. The Company is in the process of implementing those various protocol amendments. We expect to report data in children 2-5 years of age in March. If the data is supportive and subject to regulatory consultation, Moderna may proceed with regulatory filings for children 2-5 years of age thereafter. This post contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended, including regarding: the Company’s development of a vaccine against COVID-19 (mRNA-1273); the Company’s evaluation of different doses for mRNA-1273 in adolescent and pediatric populations; the evaluation of booster doses of mRNA-1273 in adolescents; and the timing for anticipated results in pediatric trials for mRNA-1273 and subsequent regulatory filings.
